verses.1: He was twenty-one years old when he became king. He ruled for fifty-five years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Hefzi-Bah.
verses.2: And he did evil in the eyes of the LORD, just as the nations had done before Jehovah, since he was a descendant of Israel.
verses.3: And he sat down and built the altars that his father Hazakiah had destroyed. He also rebuilt the idols of the gods. He did what Ahaz, the king of Israel, had done before him. He worshipped all the nations of heaven, and they served those idols.
verses.4: And I will establish a sanctuary in the house of Jehovah, which Jehovah said he would place His name there in Jerusalem.
verses.5: And he made altars for all the nations of the heavens, in two courtyards of the house of Jehovah.
verses.6: And he brought his children into the fire and the wind; he also caused them to suffer many hardships. He did all this to provoke Jehovah’s anger.
verses.7: And he set up the ark of the covenant that He made in the house. This is what the LORD said to David and to Solomon, his sons: “In this house, in Jerusalem, which I have chosen from all the tribes of Israel, I will make my name last forever.”
verses.8: And I will not allow Israel to leave the land that I gave to their ancestors, unless they keep doing everything that I have commanded them. They must also obey all the laws and regulations that Moses, my servant, commanded them.
verses.9: And they did not listen. Menashe decided to do what was evil among the nations that Jehovah had destroyed from before the children of Israel.
verses.10: And the LORD spoke through His servants, the prophets, with these words:
verses.11: For those horrible things that Manasseh, the king of Judah, did, they were worse than everything that the Amorites had done before him. He also led Judah into destruction.
verses.12: Therefore, as the Lord God of Israel says: “I will bring disaster upon Jerusalem and Judah. All those who hear this will be destroyed.”
verses.13: And I settled in Jerusalem the records of Jehoiakim and the deeds of Ahaz. I destroyed Jerusalem, just as it was destroyed by the dust from the destruction of the Temple.
verses.14: And I will give over the rest of my inheritance to them. They will be their enemies’ prey, and they will become a source of suffering and misery for all their enemies.
verses.15: Because they did evil in my eyes, and they have been angry with me since the day their ancestors left Egypt until today.
verses.16: And even pure blood was shed by many people, until Jerusalem was filled with sin. This was because their sins led them to do evil in the eyes of Jehovah.
verses.17: And all the words of Menashe, and everything he did, and his sins, are written in the book of days for the kings of Judah.
verses.18: And Menashe lay down with his fathers. He was buried in the garden of his house, in the garden of Uzza. And Amun’s son became his king.
verses.19: He was forty-one years old when he became king. He ruled in Jerusalem for twenty years. His mother’s name was Meshulamah, who was from Haruzim.
verses.20: And he did evil in the eyes of the LORD, just as his father Manasseh had done.
verses.21: And he went along all the paths that his father had walked. He served those gods whom his father had also served. And he worshiped them.
verses.22: And he abandoned Jehovah, the God of his fathers. He did not follow in Jehovah’s ways.
verses.23: And the servants of Amun bound him and killed the king in his own house.
verses.24: And the people of the land put an end to all those who opposed King Amon. They appointed Yosiah as their king.
verses.25: And the additional words of Amnon, which he said, are not written in the book of the days of the kings of Judah.
verses.26: And he placed him in his garden, in a place of peace and tranquility. And Josiah was his son, who ruled under him.
